paper_metadata.title: The microcrack inhibition and mechanical properties of an in-situ synthesized refractory high-entropy alloy fabricated by additive manufacturing

evidence.quote: Here, we selected a CrMoNbV RHEA alloy system known for its exceptional high-temperature strength but brittleness [ 13 ], and synthesized AM-processed parts in-situ using the DED technique with blended elemental powders.
The present work provides a novel microcrack inhibition method to fabricate high-performance additively manufactured RHEAs for structural applications.

Three types of feedstock powders were mechanically mixed by a planetary ball mill device (Turbula t2f, Glen Mills) with atomic ratios of Cr 25 Mo 25 Nb 25 V 25 , (Cr 25 Mo 25 Nb 25 V 25 ) 99 C 1 , (Cr 25 Mo 25 Nb 25 V 25 ) 99 C 2 .

Inspired by the grain boundary engineering in as-cast RHEAs [ 14 ], we added 1 at.% metalloid C into the CrMoNbV blended powders (named + 1C mixed powders) and conducted the DED process to obtain the + 1C DEDed RHEA via in-site alloying.

Encouragingly, microcracks in the + 1C DEDed RHEA were effectively suppressed ( Fig. 1 d). The as-built + 1C DEDed RHEA also exhibit a single BCC and equiaxed-grain morphology with average grain size of 46 μ m ( Fig. 1 e).
Additionally, 2 at.% metalloid C was added into the CrMoNbV blended powders to fabricate the + 2C DEDed RHEA ( Fig. S2 ).

Additionally, 2 at.% metalloid C was added into the CrMoNbV blended powders to fabricate the + 2C DEDed RHEA ( Fig. S2 ). While the as-built sample exhibits a single BCC structure, it contains more microcracks propagating across grains, indicating that excessive C addition (2 at.%) exacerbates thermal cracking in the DEDed RHEA due to the strong carbide-forming nature of Cr, Mo, Nb, and V, leading to brittle carbide precipitation [ 16 ].
In the following, we deeply analyzed the microstructure and mechanical properties of + 1C DEDed RHEA.
To elucidate the high-temperature deformation mechanisms of the + 1C DEDed RHEA at 1000 ◦ C, a thin foil extracted by FIB from the fractured sample was meticulously examined by TEM ( Fig. 4 ).

The resulting crack-free DEDed RHEA exhibits exceptional high-temperature proper- ties, with a yield strength surpassing 787 MPa at temperatures up to 1000 °C, outperforming other reported additively manufactured alloys.

The RHEA samples of Cr 25 Mo 25 Nb 25 V 25 RHEA with various C addition (named + 0C DEDed RHEA, + 1C DEDed RHEA and + 2C DEDed RHEA) were prepared by a DED device (LENS MR-7, Optomec), equipped with YAG fiber laser (maximum power of 1000 W, wavelength of 1064 nm) under a protective atmosphere of argon. The process parameters adopted for DED were laser power of 400 – 650 W, laser scanning speed of 4 mm/s, layer thickness of 76 μ m and a hatching distance of 305 μ m.

Compared to the original mixed powders, the DEDed RHEAs display a single set of BCC diffraction peaks, indicating the achievement of in-situ alloying during the DED process.

The as-built + 1C DEDed RHEA also exhibit a single BCC and equiaxed-grain morphology with average grain size of 46 μ m ( Fig. 1 e). Inside the grains, a dendritic and interdendritic microstructure was observed owing to compositional fluctuation ( Fig. 1 f), reminiscent of the microstructure observed in the as-cast state [ 13 ].

According to the SAED pattern, a disordered BCC structure was detected within the three regions, which kept a fully coherent orientation relationship, and no precipitates or ordered phases were detected.
Fig. 1 c presents the EBSD morphology of the + 0C DEDed RHEA surrounding a microcrack, showing an equiaxed-grain structure with an average grain size of 42 μ m.
The as-built + 1C DEDed RHEA also exhibit a single BCC and equiaxed-grain morphology with average grain size of 46 μ m ( Fig. 1 e).
Inside the grains, a dendritic and interdendritic microstructure was observed owing to compositional fluctuation ( Fig. 1 f), reminiscent of the microstructure observed in the as-cast state [ 13 ].

Further examination revealed the presence of high-density dislocations within the interdendritic region (dislocation density was estimated to be 6.07 × 10 12 m 2 ), characterized by the occurrence of long, straight screw dislocations extending from the interdendritic to the dendritic phase ( Fig. 2 g).

Conversely, the interdendrite region C displayed pronounced plastic deformation ( Fig. 4 a and d), characterized by a substantial generation of dislocations (dislocation density was estimated to be 1.15 × 10 15 m 2 ).

The deformation mechanism of interdendrite (region C) is similar to the border of dendrite (region B) ( Fig. 4 d), but the severe deformation of interdendrite facilitates its dislocation multiplication and interaction, producing abundant dislocation forests and dislocation tangles [ 27 ], which could become barriers to hinder the dislocation movement and contribute to the observed superior high-temperature strength.
In Fig. 1 b, the SEM image of + 0C DEDed RHEA in the backscattered electron (BSE) model reveals abundant microcracks and some unmelted Mo particles within the as-built RHEA.

While the as-built sample exhibits a single BCC structure, it contains more microcracks propagating across grains, indicating that excessive C addition (2 at.%) exacerbates thermal cracking in the DEDed RHEA due to the strong carbide-forming nature of Cr, Mo, Nb, and V, leading to brittle carbide precipitation [ 16 ].

This remarkable high-temperature strength is attributed to the robust pinning effect exerted on dislocations within both dendritic and inter- dendritic regions at elevated temperatures, facilitated by severe lattice distortion, local chemical fluctuations (LCFs), solute atoms, and dislo- cation interactions.

The brittleness of the grain boundaries in RHEAs is attributed to grain-boundary segregation of oxygen contaminants which weakens cohesion [ 14 ].

mechanisms.name: carbon grain boundary segregation suppressing oxygen segregation

evidence.quote: Microalloying of C atoms which preferentially segregate to grain boundaries in RHEA can suppresses the O segregation at grain boundaries, which contributes to a stronger cohesion and suppresses early intergranular crack under thermal stress [ 14 ].

Besides, the concentration of C atoms near the grain boundaries increases the solidus temperature and decreases the width of solid-liquid coexistence zone, which attributes to reduce the intergranular contraction stress during the solidification of laser-induced molten pools [ 17 ].

mechanisms.name: dislocation pinning by lattice distortion, local chemical fluctuations and solute atoms

evidence.quote: Precipitation hardening is negligible in this alloy due to the absence of precipitates during high-temperature deformation. Thus, the pronounced pinning effect exerted on the dislocations is attributed to severe local lattice distortion, local chemical fluctuations (LCFs) and solute atoms, similar to the casting CrMoNbV alloy reported before [ 13 ].

The nucleation and motion of dislocations can effectively mitigate the stress concentration and release the strain energy, consequently prevent the microcrack initiation [ 19 ].

The reduction in plasticity at 1000 ◦ C can be attributed to oxygen-induced embrittlement. Previous studies have shown that at temperatures exceeding 900 ◦ C, the evaporation of V 2 O 5 destructs the dense protective oxide scale, accelerating the internal diffusion of environmental oxygen [ 20 ].
